These altricial neonates, entirely dependent on maternal care, exhibit a modest crown-rump length of 8 centimeters [Lb = 8 centimeters] at birth, reflecting their relatively undeveloped state immediately following parturition. The gestation period that produces these litters lasts approximately 31.5 days [tg = approximately 31.5 days], a remarkably consistent duration for this strain when females are housed at a standard ambient temperature of 39 °C [T = 39 °C]. This brief intrauterine phase is typical of lagomorphs and is followed by a rapid post-natal developmental schedule, shaped by the predictable thermal environment of the laboratory setting.

The exceptional reproductive output of this strain is highlighted by a single female who produced a total of 130 offspring across five reproductive years . The animals' maximum lifespan extends to 9 years [am = 9 years] at 39 °C [T = 39 °C], a relatively long duration for a rabbit of this size, reflecting ad libitum nutrition and veterinary care.

From a comparative perspective, the ultimate crown-rump length of adults reaches 50 centimeters [Li = 50 centimeters], placing the New Zealand White among larger domestic rabbit varieties.
